profile.summary: Software engineer interested in tackling challenging problems.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Backend engineer on the Invest trading team

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Money Movement Experience 
Front end facing team focused on reducing transaction defect rates and improving overall "checkout" conversion.  Shipped user-facing screens/flows for Interac and PayTo; partnered with teams to add Klarna.  Fixed various translation related bugs and improved the language flow for users in various country corridors.  Revamped pricing vs speed presentation for Plaid. 

Global Disbursement Network
Backend team that expands out and maintains the banking network.  Implemented direct integrations with partner banks using their API specs, contributed to money movement catalogs and made improvements to the disbursement service.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Rivian Payments Platform Team - This team is focused on payment reconciliation for vehicle payments and managing any user payments.  My largest impact was to build a GDPR deidentification API orchestrating calls across internal microservices and notifying upstream systems of impacts. 

Additionally, I worked on developing the charging payments reconciliation for the Rivian Adventure Network; developed a Terraform → Glue → S3 pipeline for batched transactions and multiple Lambda functions for tax calculation/validation.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Software Engineer - Machine Learning Platform.  Helped out data science teams with implementing their projects, from model training to Airflow pipelines.  One of the coolest projects I worked on was replacing human stylist manual recommendations with ML outputs: wrote a downstream Kafka consumer and refactored a Flask service used for external/ingress calls.

projects.title: MIT Hacking Medicine - Grand Hack 2016
projects.description:
- Patients suffering from congenital heart failure (CHF) require extensive amounts of care; by strictly adhering to their medication schedule, their risk factor for readmission can be reduced.  By creating an algorithm to analyze patient data from both patient hospital and pharmacy medical records, it was possible to predict medication adherence probability, thus achieving better clinical outcomes.  
- Team won “Best EMR Hack” – InterSystems company sponsored prize.

projects.title: recoverHub - MIT Hacking Medicine 2017
projects.description:
-Goal is to develop a web portal that connects patients who suffer from opioid addiction to detox centers, halfway houses, and transitional support services.  This would also allow other treatment centers to see other options should treatment be unavailable at their center.    
-Team won Finalist prize at MIT Hacking Medicine 2017
